title: Design partner feedback log — Private upgrade + rollback (VPC + on-prem)
content:
Purpose
- Keep a running log of feedback from two design partners for the “Private upgrade + rollback mechanism” project.
- Capture: pain points, requested checks, blocked items, and follow-ups/owners.

Design partners in scope
1) Cascade Financial Group (VPC Private)
   - Regulated environment, strict change-management windows.
   - Primary concerns: deterministic rollback guarantees, audit trails, prechecks that prevent “half upgrades,” and clear upgrade window comms.

2) Northstar Health Systems (On-prem / air-gapped Private)
   - Air-gapped, offline artifact handling. Wants an “upgrade bundle” story with verification + clear remediation.
   - Primary concerns: artifact mirrors, signature/checksum errors, snapshot feasibility on their storage backend, and workable offline prerequisites.

How to use this doc
- Each entry is written as: Date / Partner / Topic / Feedback / Impact / Follow-up (owner + due date) / Status.
- If an item becomes a formal requirement, link it to a Linear ticket + note acceptance criteria.

Open questions (tracked until resolved)
- What is our minimum rollback guarantee statement (N-1 -> N only vs broader)? (Vivek + Connor)
- For on-prem, what is our “supported backup primitive” baseline when CSI snapshots aren’t available? (Irene + Fatima)
- How prescriptive should we be about upgrade windows and approvals (policy vs tooling guardrails)? (Sean + Connor)

========================================
LOG (most recent first)

2025-06-18 — Northstar (On-prem) — Offline bundle verification UX
Feedback
- They hit repeated “signature/checksum verification failed” during a dry run in their staging lab.
- Their ask: error output must show: (1) which file failed, (2) expected vs actual checksum (or signature chain status), (3) where the installer looked for the manifest, (4) a single remediation path.
- They also want an explicit ‘--skip-signature-verification’ flag, but only if accompanied by a loud risk acknowledgement + audit event.
Impact
- Blocking for beta: if verification is opaque, their operators won’t run it without Redwood PS on-call.
Follow-up
- Bruno: ensure PR-4871 messaging includes file-level details + “search paths” for bundle discovery. Due 2025-06-21. Status: in progress.
- Allison: confirm audit event fields for “verification bypass requested/confirmed.” Due 2025-06-24. Status: not started.
Notes
- They explicitly prefer “fail closed” by default; bypass only for break-glass.

2025-06-14 — Cascade (VPC) — Prechecks severity + change-management alignment
Feedback
- They want a “blocking vs warning” precheck summary that aligns with their change ticket. E.g., storage headroom must block; OIDC reachability might warn if they have a documented fallback auth method.
- They asked for a single printable artifact: upgrade plan + precheck results + risk score.
Impact
- If prechecks are noisy or inconsistent, they’ll disable them; that defeats the purpose.
Follow-up
- Kira + Sean: add a runbook section: recommended mapping of precheck failures to “rollback vs fix forward” decisions. Due 2025-06-26. Status: queued.
- Connor: confirm whether Release Eng wants a signed plan artifact (hash) for audit trails. Due 2025-06-25. Status: not started.

2025-06-12 — Northstar (On-prem) — Backup expectations vs real storage
Feedback
- Their Kubernetes storage stack doesn’t support CSI snapshots reliably (vendor plugin + inconsistent snapshot classes). They can do:
  a) filesystem-level snapshots at the SAN level (operator-run), or
  b) logical DB dump + rehydrate.
- They want Redwood tooling to support “external snapshot acknowledged” mode: installer pauses at a checkpoint, records operator confirmation + timestamp + evidence string, then continues.
Impact
- Without this, our backup story isn’t deployable for them (they can’t rely on CSI snapshots).
Follow-up
- Irene + Fatima: propose an “operator-attested snapshot” mechanism (checkpoint + required confirmation + audit event + optional attachment string). Due 2025-06-28. Status: not started.
- Vivek: validate product stance (do we support attested backups for GA, or beta-only?). Due 2025-06-20. Status: in review.

2025-06-10 — Cascade (VPC) — Auditability and evidence retention
Feedback
- They require upgrade lifecycle audit events exported to SIEM with stable event types and fields.
- Specifically asked for:
  - upgrade_started (actor, target_version, from_version, environment id)
  - prechecks_failed (failed_checks list summarized in a single field; they can parse)
  - backup_completed (backup_id/locator, method, encryption status)
  - rollback_invoked (reason, operator, stage where invoked)
  - upgrade_completed (duration, versions, plan hash)
- Retention: they keep audit logs for 1 year minimum.
Impact
- This is a gating requirement for their internal compliance sign-off.
Follow-up
- Allison + Kevin Osei: ensure events emitted (PR-29187) have stable field names + documented schema. Due 2025-06-19. Status: in progress.
- Elliot: draft customer-facing snippet: “What we log during upgrades.” Due 2025-06-27. Status: queued.

2025-06-06 — Northstar (On-prem) — Artifact mirrors and “where do you pull from?”
Feedback
- They want the installer to run a “pull test” precheck against:
  - offline container registry
  - offline chart repo (if applicable)
  - optional OS package mirror (if our node prereqs require it)
- They asked for explicit listing of required images/artifacts for a target version before change window starts.
Impact
- “Surprise pull during upgrade” is unacceptable in air-gapped.
Follow-up
- Bruno: confirm Terraform variables cover mirror endpoints and that installer precheck validates reachability/auth. (PR-1340) Due 2025-06-17. Status: done.
- Devon Price: add “artifact inventory” output to upgrade plan generator (list images/charts + digests). Due 2025-06-30. Status: not started.

2025-06-03 — Cascade (VPC) — Rollback guarantees + operator confidence
Feedback
- They asked for a clear statement: “Rollback returns both control plane + data plane to previous version, and leaves DB schema in a compatible state.”
- Their biggest fear is a rollback that leaves the system “up” but subtly broken (e.g., incompatible migrations).
- They requested a rollback drill during beta: intentionally fail mid-upgrade, then roll back, then run a validation suite.
Impact
- This is the deciding factor for whether they enroll as beta design partner.
Follow-up
- Sean + Rafael: define minimal “post-rollback health verification checklist” (API checks + DB + key jobs). Due 2025-06-18. Status: in progress.
- Michael Nguyen: confirm migration guardrails align with rollback semantics (idempotent, safe locks/timeouts). Due 2025-06-20. Status: in progress.

2025-05-29 — Northstar (On-prem) — Requested prechecks (operator view)
Feedback
- Requested mandatory prechecks (block upgrade):
  - disk/storage headroom (PV usage + etcd + db volumes)
  - version compatibility: only N-1 -> N for now (hard block)
  - kube control-plane health: nodes ready, no crashlooping core system pods
  - DNS/TLS sanity: can resolve internal endpoints; certs not expiring within 30 days
  - RBAC sanity: installer SA has required verbs
- Requested warning-only prechecks:
  - OIDC reachability (they sometimes disable during maintenance)
  - “cluster quiet” (they can schedule load shedding themselves)
Impact
- Aligns with our current direction but makes it explicit what needs to be “must block.”
Follow-up
- Sahana: validate we can test these in CI matrix (on-prem-ish fixtures). Due 2025-06-05. Status: done.
- Ethan: confirm OIDC reachability classification (warn vs block) matches control-plane requirements. Due 2025-06-07. Status: done.

2025-05-22 — Cascade (VPC) — DB migration lock timeout incident history
Feedback
- They referenced a prior incident where a migration locked tables longer than their allowed window; the upgrade had to be aborted.
- They want:
  - migration lock timeout defaults
  - a precheck that detects “long-running transactions / replication lag” (if feasible)
  - a documented “abort before migration” checkpoint
Impact
- High risk area; also overlaps with SUP-18421-type failures.
Follow-up
- Michael Nguyen: document safe migration defaults + abort point. (ties to PR-29210) Due 2025-06-10. Status: done.
- Kira: add “how to detect/mitigate lock contention” to runbook. Due 2025-06-24. Status: in progress.

2025-05-14 — Northstar (On-prem) — Maintenance window reality + human factors
Feedback
- Their operators need a clear “time estimate” for each stage (plan/prechecks/backup/cp upgrade/dp upgrade/verification).
- They asked for an “at a glance” progress bar with: current stage, elapsed time, and next step.
- They want the tool to be safe for juniors: if it fails, it should print what to do next (not “contact support”).
Impact
- Strongly influences CLI UX and runbook structure.
Follow-up
- Kenji Nakamura + DES-311: ensure CLI output is stage-based with consistent formatting and suggested next command. Due 2025-06-15. Status: in review.
- Elliot + Kira: ensure docs mirror CLI stage names 1:1. Due 2025-06-20. Status: in progress.

2025-04-30 — Cascade (VPC) — Upgrade windows + communications template
Feedback
- They asked for a customer-facing comms template they can paste into internal change tickets:
  - expected impact
  - estimated duration
  - rollback criteria
  - contact/escalation path
- They prefer “quiet hours enforcement” (tool refuses to start outside a configured window), but can accept “warn + require --force” if auditable.
Impact
- This is mostly packaging/policy, but it is a recurring enterprise blocker.
Follow-up
- Connor: confirm how “upgrade window” is enforced (Terraform vars + installer check). Due 2025-05-20. Status: done (PR-1332 covers window config; installer enforcement TBD).
- Vivek: align on whether we ship hard enforcement or soft enforcement for GA. Due 2025-06-07. Status: pending.

2025-04-18 — Kickoff — Both partners — Initial pain points (baseline)
What we heard
- Current upgrades are “too implicit” (operators don’t know what will happen until it happens).
- Precheck output is either too verbose or too opaque; they want concise summary + details on demand.
- Rollback today is mostly tribal knowledge.
- For on-prem, “offline artifact” issues are the #1 source of frustration.
- For VPC, “who approved what, when” is the #1 friction point.
Action items created
- Add upgrade plan artifact (human-readable + machine-readable) before doing anything. (ENG-4821)
- Pluggable precheck framework with severities and remediation. (ENG-4829)
- Backup orchestration with consistent checkpoints. (ENG-4838)
- Deterministic rollback command based on stored state. (ENG-4844)

========================================
Summary of top requested items (rolling)
1) Deterministic rollback with explicit checkpoints (both)
2) Strong prechecks with clear blocking vs warning classifications (both)
3) Offline artifact inventory + verification with actionable errors (Northstar)
4) Audit events with stable schemas + SIEM export compatibility (Cascade)
5) Migration guardrails and “abort before migration” story (Cascade)
6) Backup strategy that works even without CSI snapshots (Northstar)

Blocked items (current)
- On-prem: snapshot mechanism mismatch (CSI snapshots unreliable) — needs operator-attested snapshot option or documented supported alternatives.
- On-prem: signature/checksum failure remediation too opaque — needs improved UX plus break-glass path with auditing.
- VPC: definitive rollback guarantee statement pending product + release policy alignment.

Notes to self (Markus)
- Keep asking for concrete “no-go” thresholds (how much downtime? what constitutes rollback trigger?).
- Collect 2-3 real logs/screenshots from Northstar’s offline verification failures for docs.
- For Cascade, ask for a sample change ticket template so docs can match their fields exactly.
